notTheClaim: WCAG 3 is a Working Draft and is not the conformance target. APCA is a readability note, not a replacement for the 4.5:1 test.

rules: Text uses approved pairs from tokens/sparq-tokens.json contrast.
Accent text sits on the ground, not on the off-white ink.
State is never color alone. An accent hairline sits next to a word or aria-current.
Focus ring and the active hairline need 3:1 against the adjacent ground.
Tab order follows the visual order.
On a new build, a composite such as the section rail keeps one tab stop and uses arrow keys inside.
On an existing app, rebuilding tab order is a suggestion, not an adoption edit.
Focus is a 2px accent outline, offset so it stays visible, and is not covered by a sticky column.
There is no keyboard trap.
A skip link is required when a view has more than one landmark.
Hit areas are at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, using min-size or padding when the visible label is smaller.
prefers-reduced-motion jumps arrivals to the end state and paints orbs as one still frame.
Orbs can be paused.
prefers-contrast: more and forced-colors keep hairlines and focus visible.
An orb is never the only status.
On a new build, streaming or regenerated copy uses aria-live polite.
Errors that block the next step use assertive once, not on every token.
Focus does not jump to a region that updated itself.
Orbs and other canvases are aria-hidden. The text state is the name.
A percent, a color ramp, or motion alone is never the confidence signal.
On an existing app, adding a live region or changing when focus moves is a suggestion.

apca.role: readability note for small mono on a dark ground
